phase.text: Pivotal trial; CAPS is an orphan disease with too few patients for two independent randomized trials, so one pivotal trial was performed.

citations.quote: CAPS is an Orphan disease with too few patients available to conduct two independent randomized clinical trials. Therefore, one pivotal trial was performed. This trial analyzed the same study population, first in a double-blind, placebo-controlled phase (Part A), and then in a withdrawal phase (Part B) after re-randomization, when all subjects had been on rilonacept for 9 or 15 weeks. A total of 47 CAPS patients were studied in the pivotal trial. An additional 42 subjects with CAPS were studied in the development program. In all 600 subjects have been treated with rilonacept. A total of 85 and 65 subjects have been treated at the 160 mg dose for 6 months and one year, respectively.

indication.text: ARCALYST (rilonacept) is an interleukin-1 blocker indicated for the treatment of Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS), including Familial Cold Autoinflammatory Syndrome (FCAS) and Muckle-Wells Syndrome (MWS) in adults and children 12 and older.

citations.quote: ARCALYST (rilonacept) is an interleukin-1 blocker indicated for the treatment of Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS), including Familial Cold Autoinflammatory Syndrome (FCAS) and Muckle-Wells Syndrome (MWS) in adults and children 12 and older. (1)

target_moa.text: Rilonacept is a dimeric fusion protein of the extracellular domains of the IL-1 Type I receptor and IL-1 receptor accessory protein fused to the Fc portion of human IgG1; it binds IL-1 and interferes with its interaction with the receptor, countering the uncontrolled overproduction of IL-1 that drives inflammation in CAPS.

citations.quote: The pathogenesis of CAPS is thought to be due to uncontrolled overproduction and release of IL-1, with resultant inflammation. Rilonacept is a dimeric fusion protein consisting of the extracellular domains of the IL-1 (interleukin-1) Type I receptor and the IL-1 receptor accessory protein fused to the Fc portion of human IgG1. Rilonacept binds IL-1, interfering with its interaction with the recept

Arcalyst, generic name rilonacept, is an interleukin-1 (IL-1) antagonist. Rilonacept is a fusion protein that consists of the human IL-1 receptor extracellular domains and the Fc portion of human IgG1. This new molecular entity binds IL-1 thereby inhibiting the cytokine. Rilonacept is administered subcutaneously.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions are injection-site reactions and upper respiratory tract infections. Injection-site reactions occurred in 48% (Part A) and 36% (Part B withdrawal) of rilonacept patients vs 13% placebo. Infections risk is a class effect of IL-1 antagonism; coadministration with TNF blockers should be avoided.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions reported by patients with CAPS treated with ARCALYST are injection-site reactions and upper respiratory tract infections. (6.2, 6.3)
